header:
Date: 2025-05-01
Time: 15:00 - 16:02 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Location: Zoom
Meeting recorded: yes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Marcus Ng (Redwood SE), Riley Brooks (Redwood CSM), Sofia Patel (Marigold Head of Procurement), Evan Rios (Marigold Security Architect), Diane Cho (Marigold Legal), Tom Beckett (Marigold CTO), Marta Vela (Marigold ML Platform)
summary: Procurement and legal intake to align on MSA/DPA items, SLA expectations, pricing pathways (hosted vs dedicated vs private), KMS/HSM integration and pilot success criteria. Agreed to pilot, Redwood to provide bench artifacts and updated term sheet. Legal to review DPA redlines.
topics: MSA redlines, DPA data residency, SLA targets (p99 latency), pricing ladder and egress, reserved capacity (Dedicated) vs Hosted, Private (VPC/on-prem) constraints, KMS/HSM integration, SOC 2 evidence, pilot scope and benchmarks
transcript:
[00:00] Lena Ortiz: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick go round for names?
[00:05] Sofia Patel: Sofia here, head of procurement at Marigold.
[00:08] Tom Beckett: Tom, CTO.
[00:10] Diane Cho: Diane, legal counsel.
[00:12] Evan Rios: Evan, information security.
[00:14] Marta Vela: Marta, ML platform.
[00:16] Marcus Ng: Marcus, solutions engineer, Redwood.
[00:18] Riley Brooks: Riley, CSM.
[00:20] Lena Ortiz: Great. Agenda: MSA/DPA redlines, SLA targets, pricing for pilot and production, and next steps. We'll keep this tight.
[01:02] Sofia Patel: High level, procurement wants to understand the acceptance criteria — when do we consider the pilot successful and who signs off for production? Also pricing ceilings — we need an expected unit cost.
[01:15] Marcus Ng: For pilots we usually recommend a 2-4 week bench plus integration window. Bench should cover latency, throughput, and correctness on your prompt set. We'll provide a script and the sample data flow. Success is: p95 latency under agreed SLO for 95% of synthetic load, throughput target met, and no leakage of customer data.
[01:40] Marta Vela: Quick note — our model infra team cares about KV cache warmup and consistent latency for short inference (few tokens). If you do batching aggressively we can see latency spikes.
[01:55] Marcus Ng: Yep absolutely — we'll include continuous-batching settings and a recommended config. Also we have prefix caching and KV-cache management, sometimes mis-typed in notes as K V cache, but same thing.
[02:10] Evan Rios: From security: we need details on encryption at rest and in-flight, KMS integration, tenant separation, and audit logs. Also curious about private deployment options — can Redwood run in our VPC or on-prem?
[02:30] Lena Ortiz: Good question. We support Hosted API, Dedicated reserved GPU capacity, and Private deployments (VPC and on-prem). For Private we offer a customer-controlled control plane and KMS integration. Marcus, can you expand on keying?
[02:42] Marcus Ng: Sure. For Hosted we support envelope encryption and bring-your-own-key via Redwood-managed KMS or customer KMS through a connector (we call it KMS bridge). For Dedicated we can integrate with your KMS over an HSM-backed keywrap or use a Cloud KMS with restricted key usage. For Private on-prem, you can bring your own HSM. There are some network and bootstrap steps — we'll share the KMS onboarding doc.
[03:10] Diane Cho: On the DPA: we need to ensure data residency for EU PHI-type records — can Redwood commit to not transfer data outside EU for EU customers?
[03:22] Lena Ortiz: We have region pinning and can commit to regional processing for private deployments; for Hosted we have EU regions — Marcus, is regional data residency a standard clause?
[03:30] Marcus Ng: It's doable; Hosted customers can pin to EU region, logs and telemetry can be kept in-region depending on plan. For absolute legal guarantees we recommend Private deployment or Dedicated capacity with contractual clauses in the MSA/DPA.
[03:48] Tom Beckett: Pricing. We are trying to understand cost of tokens plus egress and reserved options. We run high-volume embedding and generation workloads. If we go Dedicated, what's the delta versus hosted?
[04:02] Lena Ortiz: High-level: Hosted is variable per-token pricing; Dedicated is a committed monthly cost that gives predictable throughput and lower unit cost at scale. There's also egress considerations for models served in certain regions — we can model sample numbers for you. Marcus can show a ladder.
[04:18] Marcus Ng: I'll put together a sample ladder. Example: at 50M tokens/month hosted might be $X/token; Dedicated with a 3-node pool drops unit to ~Y/token but you pay commit. We also account for model variants and quantization savings. Egress fees — depends on cloud region and inter-region transfer, we'll include that in the sheet.
[04:48] Diana? Diane Cho: DPA redlines we currently have: deletion guarantees, subprocessors list, audit rights, breach notifications timeline (48 hours preferred), and liability caps. Can Redwood accept 48 hours?
[05:02] Lena Ortiz: Standard Redwood breach window is 72 hours; we can escalate for enterprise customers. We will flag that for legal.
[05:12] Diane Cho: Ok flag it, but we might push to 48. Also need SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 evidence.
[05:20] Marcus Ng: We can share SOC 2 reports via an NDA; ISO 27001 — many customers ask, we'll confirm certification details in the security pack.
[05:34] Evan Rios: Audit logs — rotation and retention. We want 12 months of detailed audit logs for privileged ops. Is that supported?
[05:44] Riley Brooks: We have log retention options in the console; for enterprise plans you can increase retention and export logs to your SIEM via secure shipping.
[05:52] Marta Vela: On private deployment, how does upgrade and patching work? We want reproducible binary hashes and a maintenance window.
[06:02] Marcus Ng: Private and Dedicated both have a deployment orchestration — we push signed artifacts and provide an upgrade schedule; for on-prem the customer opts in to the maintenance window and we supply signed packages and SLSA-ish provenance metadata.
[06:20] Tom Beckett: Good. Another point — model fallback. If our primary variant is constrained, will the call route to a cheaper model automatically? We need deterministic behavior.
[06:30] Marcus Ng: Smart routing can fallback to compatible model variants per policy — you can set routing to prefer latency or cost. For deterministic production behavior we recommend explicit pinning for critical routes and a controlled fallback policy for non-critical routes.
[06:45] Sofia Patel: Timeline — procurement wants to close terms and pilot pricing this week if possible. Legal and security need artifacts. Are you able to hit that?
[06:55] Lena Ortiz: We'll try. Action plan: we'll send a redlined MSA proposal (markups), the DPA with suggested compromises, and a pilot pricing proposal. Marcus will send benchmark scripts and the pilot runbook.
[07:08] Diane Cho: One small item — data deletion on termination. We need proof — do you provide deletion certificates?
[07:16] Marcus Ng: We provide a termination checklist and can provide a signed attest to data deletion for Private/Dedicated. Hosted may have a standardized process, we can provide confirmation of deletion and log of actions.
[07:28] Evan Rios: KMS: we need a threat model. Does Redwood keep plaintext keys? Where are keys stored when using your KMS bridge?
[07:38] Marcus Ng: Keys are never stored in plaintext. The KMS bridge uses a key-wrapping flow; for BYOK we only store wrapped keys. For Hosted with customer-managed KMS we maintain minimal metadata to support rotation, but not plaintext material.
[07:55] Marta Vela: For the pilot we want to run two scenarios: 1) hosted quickstart to validate correctness, 2) Dedicated small-footprint pilot to validate throughput and caching. Estimated load 100 qps burst, average 10 qps, sequences ~32 tokens.
[08:10] Marcus Ng: That works. We'll provide config advice: concurrent workers, batching thresholds, and KV-cache warmup. Also note that very short sequences can be bottlenecked by RPC overhead; we recommend small sequence bundling in the bench.
[08:26] Tom Beckett: Any regulatory issues for PHI? We need to know whether Redwood signs BAAs or supports HIPAA?
[08:36] Lena Ortiz: Redwood offers an enterprise compliance package; BAAs are supported under private deployments and certain enterprise plans. We'll surface the BAA language and limitations.
[08:50] Diane Cho: SLA specifics: we need an uptime SLA and a p99 latency commitment for production endpoints. Typical ask: 99.9% uptime and p99 under 500ms for short sequences. Can you commit?
[09:05] Marcus Ng: For Hosted we aim for 99.9% but depends on region and plan; p99 500ms depends heavily on sequence length and model. For short sequences with Dedicated and tuned batching we can often meet p99 < 500ms. We'll put specific SLO numbers in the proposal and call out caveats for model size and quantization.
[09:30] Sofia Patel: Pricing approvals: we need an example cost for a 3-month pilot and a forecast into production with both hosted vs dedicated scenarios. Is there a standard pilot discount?
[09:42] Lena Ortiz: We generally offer pilot credits or a discount on the first 3 months for committed pilots, depending on scope. We'll put options in the pricing sheet.
[09:55] Diane Cho: On liability caps: our procurement typically wants a higher cap for data breaches; what's Redwood's posture?
[10:03] Lena Ortiz: Redwood has a standard commercial liability cap; for enterprise we can discuss raising it under negotiated terms. This will be handled in MSA negotiation.
[10:14] Marcus Ng: Technical note — for dedicated pools we can provision GPU types that match your throughput needs; we'll recommend instance sizes in the bench results. Also quantized model variants can significantly reduce cost and latency — we'll include a recommendation per workload.
[10:30] Marta Vela: Does Redwood support A/B rollouts and canary tests controlled from the console? We want to do gradual rollout for model changes.
[10:38] Riley Brooks: Yes, the Console supports canary/A-B rollouts, traffic splitting, and automatic rollback policies. We'll show a short demo in the next technical session.
[10:50] Evan Rios: Data access: who at Redwood can access PII? We need strict RBAC.
[10:57] Marcus Ng: Access is role-based and audited; privileged access is limited and logged. For sensitive customers we can gate operations via a privileged access process and require explicit approvals.
[11:10] Diane Cho: Can you share a sample subprocessor list? Procurement needs it to evaluate third-party risks.
[11:16] Lena Ortiz: We'll share our current subprocessor list; it's included in the security pack. Expect cloud infra partners and CDN providers listed.
[11:25] Tom Beckett: Egress again — if we pin region EU and export embeddings to our analytics cluster in US, what fees apply?
[11:33] Marcus Ng: Cross-region egress fees apply per provider and typically per GB. We'll model it for your expected traffic and include a sensitivity analysis.
[11:45] Sofia Patel: Ok let's align deadlines: legal to review and send redlines by Friday 2025-05-08, Redwood to return updated term sheet and pilot pricing by 2025-05-05, pilot kick-off week of 2025-05-12.
[12:00] Lena Ortiz: Confirmed. Anything else from Marigold?
[12:06] Diane Cho: One more — we want to keep training data separate from inference telemetry. How is telemetry handled?
[12:12] Marcus Ng: Telemetry is collected for performance and error monitoring; we can separate training artifacts and exclude telemetry from being used to train models. We'll put a contractual clause in the DPA if needed.
[12:26] Marta Vela: For benchmarking can you provide a script that runs token-level latency and measures KV cache hits?
[12:33] Marcus Ng: Yes — bench script, sample dataset, and a bench spreadsheet with expected counters.
[12:40] Sofia Patel: Great. Recap?
[12:45] Lena Ortiz: Recap — Redwood sends MSA/DPA redlines and security pack; Marcus sends pilot runbook and bench scripts; Marigold legal to provide DPA redlines and required clauses; schedule pilot kickoff week of 2025-05-12. Next meeting — technical pilot kick-off (Marcus + Marta + Tom) proposed 2025-05-13.
[12:58] Tom Beckett: Sounds good.
[13:00] Lena Ortiz: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with links. Meeting ends.
